sources.title: Luc Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, Chapter II: Inversion Method
sources.locator: Complete 56-page chapter PDF inspected; §§2.1–2.2, printed pp. 27–35 (PDF pp. 1–7): inversion principle, numerical inversion caveat, bisection procedure, and stopping criterion.

contents.name: §2.1 Inversion principle and generalized inverse
contents.support: The inversion threshold characterization supports the infimum convention; local proof verifies nonemptiness, boundedness, right continuity, and the sublevel equivalence.

contents.name: §2.2 Numerical inversion by bisection
contents.support: The numerical inversion discussion motivates bracketed bisection and its finite stopping rule; the carrier makes exact comparisons, modulus, budget, and tail status explicit.

contents.name: §2.2 Numerical inversion error caveat
contents.support: The source warns numerical inversion need not be exact; the carrier proves residual, density-conditioned spatial, and fixed-grid distribution bounds.

contents.name: §2.2 Error near a vanishing density
contents.support: The local F(x)=x^2 example verifies that CDF residual alone gives only square-root spatial control near zero.

sources.title: Luc Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, Chapter III: Discrete Distributions
sources.locator: Complete 35-page chapter PDF inspected; §§2.1 and 2.3, printed pp. 85–89: discrete inversion and binary search.

contents.name: §2.1 Discrete inversion
contents.support: Cumulative probabilities and inverse-CDF selection support the finite categorical procedure; binary search is bounded by the number of comparisons.

contents.name: §2.1 Exact categorical probabilities
contents.support: The interval masses are cumulative-threshold differences; the carrier derives exact ideal frequencies and midpoint-grid rounding errors.

contents.name: §2.3 Binary search for a discrete inverse
contents.support: The selected cumulative threshold can be found by binary search in the sorted cumulative array.

sources.title: Luc Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, Chapter V: Normal Variates
sources.locator: Complete 40-page chapter PDF inspected; §4.4, printed pp. 235–236 (PDF pp. 1–2): polar/Box–Muller normal-generation method.

contents.name: §4.4 Polar method and Box–Muller transform
contents.support: The Box–Muller formula is supported; the carrier supplies a full change-of-variables proof of its product Gaussian density, radial tail, and second moment.

contents.name: §4.4 Independent normal outputs
contents.support: The source describes the normal transform; the carrier combines the locally proved law with independent uniforms from disjoint bit streams.

contents.name: §4.4 Finite precision and tails
contents.support: The source supplies the exact reference transform; the carrier separately proves finite midpoint and evaluator-error bounds and states the finite-support TV limitation.

contents.name: §4.4 Midpoint radial cutoff and zero endpoint
contents.support: The example computes the exact-real reference radius cutoff from the smallest midpoint and the Rayleigh tail.

contents.name: §4.4 Endpoint convention for logarithm input
contents.support: The example contrasts a raw grid containing zero with the strictly positive midpoint grid.

contents.name: §4.4 Finite midpoint inputs and certified evaluator interface
contents.support: The source supplies the exact Box–Muller formula implemented by the carrier; the carrier states deterministic log, square-root, and trigonometric evaluator contracts and returns inconclusive when certification fails.

sources.title: Luc Devroye, Non-Uniform Random Variate Generation, Chapter XV: The Random Bit Model
sources.locator: Complete 38-page chapter PDF downloaded and inspected; §§1.1–1.2, printed pp. 769–778: random-bit model, Bernoulli comparison, and rejection example.

contents.name: §1.1 Random bit model and ideal fair bits
contents.support: The source distinguishes ideal fair-bit inputs from an available real uniform oracle; the carrier constructs the infinite-bit uniform and disjoint-stream independence from product-space suppliers.

contents.name: §1.2 Bernoulli generation from bits
contents.support: The source gives bit-by-bit Bernoulli and rejection constructions; the carrier specializes to unbiased rational Bernoulli sampling with explicit capped failure.

contents.name: §1.2 Rejection probability and bit cost
contents.support: The source motivates rejection from finite bit blocks; the carrier sums exact first-acceptance probabilities and derives the geometric expected cost.

contents.name: §1.1 Ideal stream versus finite output caveat
contents.support: The source separates an ideal infinite random-bit model from finite computation; the carrier proves midpoint coupling, CDF, Wasserstein, and maximal TV bounds.

sources.title: Pierre L’Ecuyer, Pseudorandom Number Generators (2007)
sources.locator: Historical full-text harvest: the complete author PDF was downloaded and read locally (printed pp. 1–13), but the current author URL did not pass the required source-fetch stamp. The exact sections inspected were Introduction; Streams and Substreams; Quality Criteria and Testing; Linear Recurrences; Nonlinear Generators; What to Look For and What to Avoid.

contents.name: Introduction: ideal IID uniforms and finite-state RNG model
contents.support: The article defines a generator by finite states, seed distribution, transition, and output, and proves eventual repetition from finiteness; the item supplies the complete pigeonhole proof.

contents.name: Streams and substreams
contents.support: The section motivates reproducible disjoint deterministic streams; the carrier states a keyed finite-permutation interface with an explicit no-wrap exhaustion status.

contents.name: Quality criteria and testing: period does not imply independence
contents.support: The article warns that long period and good one-time coverage do not establish independent successive outputs; the local LCG theorem gives an exact dependent-pair witness.

contents.name: Linear recurrences and LCG midpoint output
contents.support: The recurrence and midpoint output transformation agree with the carrier’s exact finite-state definition.

contents.name: Linear recurrences: full-period versus adjacent dependence
contents.support: The source motivates that period and marginal uniformity do not preclude structure; the example computes a full-period cycle with deterministic parity alternation.

contents.name: Nonlinear generators and computational unpredictability
contents.reason: Cryptographic unpredictability and nonlinear generator design are outside T21; the counter-stream definition explicitly makes no cryptographic or pseudorandomness claim.

contents.name: What to look for and what to avoid; statistical tests are not proofs
contents.support: The item remarks explicitly that a supplied permutation implies no IID or cryptographic guarantee; empirical testing is not used as a proof of independence.

alternatives.argument: The item gives the full pigeonhole proof: among N+1 states two coincide; determinism propagates the repeat, and injectivity removes any preperiod. This directly proves every claim attributed to this source.

The item is a complete deterministic interface definition: it specifies finite set, key-indexed bijection, nonwrapping counter interval, output and exhaustion. The checked Random123 full paper independently motivates the counter/key design; no distribution or independence claim is imported.

The item proves the power-of-two case locally by the affine iterate, induction on powers of two, least-return divisibility, and graph-support count. Its complete prime-factor argument cites the published FTA statement to classify divisors of 2^w. Jung Theorem 3.6 is an independent full-period treatment; the adjacent-dependence claim is verified by the local support count.

The item states the exact recurrence, residue convention, seed input and midpoint output transformation. Jung §3.1 independently states the LCG recurrence; no L’Ecuyer theorem is needed for the definition.

The item directly computes the eight-state cycle 0,1,6,7,4,5,2,3,0 and reduces the recurrence modulo two to prove parity alternates; the cited local full-period theorem and finite-uniform definition prove the marginal/dependence claims.

The item proves the midpoint coupling from the exact binary tail, derives strict and non-strict CDF bounds from interval lengths, obtains the Wasserstein bound from the coupling, and witnesses total variation one using the finite grid support. Devroye Chapter XV supplies an independent ideal-bit model treatment.

sources.title: John K. Salmon, Mark A. Moraes, Ron O. Dror, and David E. Shaw, Parallel Random Numbers: As Easy as 1, 2, 3
sources.locator: Complete 12-page conference paper fetched; §2 counter-based design and the testing discussion inspected.

contents.name: §2 Counter-based generator interface and keyed bijection
contents.support: The source’s counter/key design motivates the deterministic counter interface; the carrier declares a bijection as an input contract and stops at interval exhaustion.

contents.name: §2 Distinct counters and no reuse under a permutation
contents.support: Injectivity of a fixed-key permutation gives distinct outputs for distinct counters; the carrier proves this without inferring independence.

contents.name: Statistical testing of generator families
contents.support: The carrier explicitly leaves statistical behavior unspecified, so empirical test results are not used to assert IID behavior.

sources.title: J. Jung, Monte-Carlo Methods
sources.locator: Complete 7-page course handout inspected; §3.1 and Theorem 3.6 (Hull–Dobell LCG period conditions), and §4.1 rejection sampling.

contents.name: §3.1 Linear congruential recurrence
contents.support: The course notes define the linear congruential recurrence used by the carrier.

contents.name: Theorem 3.6 Hull–Dobell full-period criterion
contents.support: The theorem provides an independent treatment of full-period conditions; the carrier proves the power-of-two case directly and adds the dependence counterclaim.

contents.name: §4.1 Rejection sampling
contents.support: The notes describe rejection and its acceptance mechanism; the carrier gives the exact rational bit-block implementation and finite-cap status.

contents.name: §4.1 Acceptance-cost discussion
contents.support: The local theorem supplies the exact geometric failure probability and expectation for the rational Bernoulli specialization.

sources.title: E. M. Raz, Lecture Notes in Probability
sources.locator: Complete 159-page lecture-note PDF inspected; §5.8, printed pp. 102–105 (PDF pp. 108–112): multivariate change of variables, polar coordinates, and Exercise 5.2 Box–Muller.

contents.name: §5.8 Change of variables and polar-coordinate Jacobian
contents.support: The notes state the multivariate substitution formula and polar Jacobian used in the Box–Muller transform; the carrier proves the map is a diffeomorphism on the slit plane and computes its determinant.

contents.name: Exercise 5.2 Box–Muller construction
contents.support: The exercise presents the transform from independent uniforms to normal coordinates; the carrier supplies the full product-density proof and then composes with fair-bit uniforms.

contents.name: §5.8 Gaussian marginal and independence calculation
contents.support: Factorization of the bivariate density into normalized one-dimensional factors gives independent standard-normal coordinates; the carrier derives normalization using Tonelli.
